capabilities.target: Supabase Postgres via service role (bypasses row level security); reachable tables include support tickets and integration_tokens
support_messages table; inserted rows are rendered back to the customer

inputs.source: Developer's direct prompt in the IDE
Customer-submitted ticket message via the public support widget, stored in the database and later read by the agent

instructions.evidence_locator: runtime notes: 'database connection uses the service role, which bypasses row level security'
instructions.note: Nothing scopes which tables a query may touch once the agent holds service-role credentials, so a benign developer request ('show me open tickets') sits on the same unrestricted credential as any other query, including reads of the integration_tokens table.

elements.name: integration_tokens table (reachable via service role, bypasses RLS)

controls.name: IDE per-tool-call approval prompt showing the SQL
controls.decay_rationale: The gate is enforced by the IDE client outside the model before every tool call, so it does not weaken as the model becomes more capable. Per control_decay.md, raw-action gates instead decay with approval volume (SAFE-T1403 consent-fatigue), which the dependence field cannot represent; see the findings' residual_rationale for how that is scored.

controls.name: Row-level-security scoped database role for execute_sql
controls.decay_rationale: A role that enforces RLS and excludes the integration_tokens table would make that table structurally unreachable from ticket-triggered queries regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Pin the Supabase MCP server to an exact version or hash
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning prevents the published package from changing tool behavior between runs without review (SAFE-T1201), independent of model capability.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted ticket content drives a service-role read of integration tokens and a customer-visible write

attack_path.note: Customer submits ticket content through the public support widget; attacker-controlled and untrusted.
Agent runs execute_sql as service role, bypassing RLS; a hidden instruction in the ticket text can redirect the read toward other tables.
Integration tokens become available in the agent's context with no RLS isolation.
Agent inserts a reply into support_messages containing the harvested data; the row is shown back to the customer, completing exfiltration across the trust boundary.

findings.residual_rationale: The approval gate is classified raw_action (it shows the SQL), which per rubric step 2 would credit -2 tiers with no moderate floor, i.e. a formal floor of moderate. The runtime notes state developers approve many calls per session, and an insert into support_messages or a broad select looks routine next to ordinary ticket-handling queries, so the gate does not reliably catch the semantic intent of an injected query. This is the approval-fatigue failure mode (SAFE-T1403) that control_decay.md flags for raw-action gates and that this case is drawn from as a real incident. Residual is therefore held at high rather than dropped to the formal moderate floor.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval gate removed or changed from per-call to session-level/always-allow; or median approved tool calls per developer session rising while review stays per-call (approval fatigue).

evidence.locator: runtime notes: 'database connection uses the service role, which bypasses row level security'
evidence.observation: Service role access makes every table, including integration_tokens, reachable from any query path, including one triggered by customer-controlled ticket content.

evidence.locator: runtime notes: 'customers write ticket messages through the public support widget... rows in support_messages are shown back to the customer'
evidence.observation: support_messages is a customer-visible egress channel, completing source-read-sink across the trust boundary.

evidence.locator: runtime notes: 'client asks the developer to approve each tool call and shows the SQL... developers approve many calls in a session'
evidence.observation: The only control on this path is a per-call human approval gate; stated high session volume is the approval-fatigue condition under which this class of attack has succeeded in practice.

recommendations.action: Use a role for execute_sql that enforces row level security so ticket-triggered reads cannot reach integration_tokens or other unrelated tables.
Separate the read path from the customer-visible write path into different credentials/tools, with a distinct, destination-naming approval step before any insert into support_messages.
Scan outbound support_messages content for secret-shaped strings (tokens, keys) before the row becomes visible to the customer.
Treat ticket text returned from execute_sql as untrusted data, never as instructions, in any downstream prompting.

findings.title: ASI04 supply chain: unpinned Supabase MCP server (@latest) allows silent tool redefinition

attack_path.note: Server is launched via npx with the @latest tag and no pin or hash check, so the running code can change between sessions without review.
A compromised or updated server binary could alter what execute_sql actually does while still presenting plausible SQL to the approval prompt.
The same broad service-role credential could be used by a compromised server to write or exfiltrate through support_messages regardless of what is shown for approval.

threat_refs.name: Publish Poisoned AI Artifacts: AI Agent Tools

findings.residual_rationale: The approval gate formally covers both capabilities and would mechanically credit -2 tiers (floor moderate, raw_action so no floor restriction). That credit is not applied here because the threat is precisely that a compromised server binary can execute different behavior than what it displays for approval, which breaks the raw_action assumption that the shown SQL reflects the real action. No other control addresses package integrity (definitions_pinned is false), so residual is kept at the inherent critical level.

evidence.observation: The MCP server is resolved at the @latest tag rather than a pinned version or hash, so its tool definitions and binary behavior can change silently between invocations.

recommendations.action: Pin the MCP server to an exact version or content hash and review diffs before any upgrade.

rating.rationale: Both findings start at critical: an untrusted customer ticket can drive a service-role read that bypasses row level security and reach the integration_tokens table, then a customer-visible write completes exfiltration; separately, the MCP server is pulled at @latest with no pinning, so its behavior is not guaranteed stable. The only present control is a per-call human approval gate that shows raw SQL. For the injection path its credit is reduced (not eliminated) by stated high per-session approval volume, consistent with the real approval-fatigue incident this case is drawn from, giving a residual of high. For the supply-chain path the gate's protection does not meaningfully apply, because a compromised server could act differently than what it displays, so that finding stays at critical, and the agent-level residual rolls up to critical. Forecast remains critical because loosening or removing the approval gate (autonomy_increase, control_removal) or longer sessions increasing fatigue (longer_task_horizon) restores full inherent severity with no mitigating control in place.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.
No system prompt was provided; instruction-level findings are limited to what the runtime notes describe.
The real RLS configuration, credential scope, and integration_tokens schema were not independently verified; they are taken as declared in the runtime notes (evidence_basis: declared).

Whether the IDE's approval prompt would actually surface an injected, token-harvesting query as suspicious was not tested; the approval-fatigue judgment is based on the stated high call volume, not an observed transcript.
